name: Fraud Investigation Procedure
description: End-to-end operational procedure for investigating fraud incidents within FirstUK Bank. Owned by the Head of Financial Crime and executed by the Financial Crime Team in coordination with Risk and Legal departments. Effective from 2026-01-15 with annual review cycle.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Team, Risk, Compliance, Legal

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: Senior leadership role responsible for owning and overseeing the Fraud Investigation Procedure. Accountable for procedure governance, updates, and departmental compliance.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: Operational team responsible for executing fraud investigations and managing fraud detection and response activities. Primary audience and executor of this procedure.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Team, Risk, Compliance, Legal

name: Risk Department
description: Risk management function coordinating with Financial Crime Team on fraud investigation procedures and risk assessment outcomes.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Team, Risk, Compliance, Legal

name: Legal Department
description: Legal function providing guidance and oversight on fraud investigation procedures, regulatory compliance, and legal obligations.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Team, Risk, Compliance, Legal

name: Compliance Function
description: Compliance oversight function responsible for ensuring fraud investigation procedures meet regulatory and policy requirements.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Team, Risk, Compliance, Legal

name: Fraud Investigation
description: The core operational activity governed by this procedure — the investigation, analysis, and resolution of suspected fraud incidents affecting FirstUK Bank customers and accounts.

name: Fraud Investigation Process
description: End-to-end procedure for investigating suspected fraud cases with standardized documentation, escalation protocols, and law enforcement coordination. Establishes the framework for thorough case handling and appropriate response actions.
context: Establish standardized procedures for investigating suspected fraud cases
ensuring thorough documentation, appropriate escalation, and coordinated response with law enforcement

name: Fraud Detection Obligation
description: The triggering event or obligation that initiates the fraud investigation process when suspected fraud is identified. Serves as the entry point for case investigation and documentation.
context: Establish standardized procedures for investigating suspected fraud cases

name: Fraud Investigation Team
description: The team responsible for conducting fraud investigations, maintaining documentation, and coordinating escalation and law enforcement response as defined in the standardized procedures.
context: appropriate escalation, and coordinated response with law enforcement

name: Fraud Investigation Documentation Checkpoint
description: Mandatory control point ensuring thorough documentation of all fraud investigation activities, findings, and decisions. Verifies that investigation records meet regulatory and internal policy requirements before case closure or escalation.
context: standardized procedures for investigating suspected fraud cases

name: Law Enforcement Coordination Checkpoint
description: Mandatory control point verifying appropriate coordination and reporting to law enforcement when fraud investigation findings warrant external notification or joint investigation.
context: appropriate escalation, and coordinated response with law enforcement

name: Fraud Investigation Framework
description: FirstUK Bank's comprehensive framework for identifying, categorizing, and investigating fraud incidents across multiple fraud types including account takeover, unauthorized transactions, check fraud, card fraud, impersonation, internal collusion, and AML/sanctions evasion. The framework establishes typical loss ranges for each fraud category to guide investigation prioritization and response.
context: FirstUK Bank fraud typically falls into:

name: Account Takeover Fraud
description: Fraud scenario where a fraudster gains unauthorized access to a customer account and transfers funds. Typical loss range for FirstUK Bank is £500–£5,000 per incident.
context: Account Takeover | Fraudster gains access to customer account, transfers funds | £500–£5,000

name: Unauthorized Transaction Fraud
description: Fraud category where a customer claims a transaction on their account was not authorized by them. Typical loss range for FirstUK Bank is £200–£10,000 per incident.
context: Unauthorized Transaction | Customer claims transaction not authorized | £200–£10,000

name: Check Fraud
description: Fraud involving stolen or forged checks that are deposited into accounts. Typical loss range for FirstUK Bank is £1,000–£50,000 per incident.

name: Card Fraud
description: Fraud where a card number is stolen and used for unauthorized online or retail transactions. Typical loss range for FirstUK Bank is £100–£5,000 per incident.
context: Card Fraud | Card number stolen, used for online/retail | £100–£5,000

name: Impersonation Fraud
description: Fraud where a fraudster opens an account using a false identity. Typical loss range for FirstUK Bank is £1,000–£20,000 per incident.
context: Impersonation | Fraudster opens account using false identity | £1,000–£20,000

name: Internal Collusion Fraud
description: Fraud facilitated by a FirstUK Bank employee working in collusion with external fraudsters or customers. Typical loss range for FirstUK Bank is £5,000–£500,000 per incident.

name: AML/Sanctions Evasion Fraud
description: Fraud where a customer deliberately evades AML and sanctions screening controls. Typical loss range for FirstUK Bank is £1,000–£1M+ per incident.
context: AML/Sanctions Evasion | Customer deliberately evades screening | £1,000–£1M+

name: Fraud Detection and Intake Process
description: End-to-end process for identifying and initiating investigation of fraudulent activity across four discovery channels: automated detection via the Fraud Detection Engine, customer reports of unauthorized transactions, internal staff observations, and law enforcement referrals. The process captures how fraud is discovered, routed, and prepared for investigation.
context: Fraud Detection Engine (FDE) flags transaction (97%+ detection rate)
Customer calls: 'I didn't authorize this transaction'

name: Automated Fraud Detection
description: Automated detection step where the Fraud Detection Engine monitors transactions and flags suspicious activity with a 97%+ detection rate. System alerts trigger investigation when anomalies are identified, such as multiple rapid international transfers.
context: Fraud Detection Engine (FDE) flags transaction (97%+ detection rate)

name: Customer-Reported Fraud Detection
description: Detection step initiated when a customer proactively reports unauthorized transactions or suspicious account activity. Customers may call to dispute charges, report unauthorized activity, or identify discrepancies on statements.
context: Customer calls: 'I didn't authorize this transaction'

name: Internal Staff Fraud Detection
description: Detection step where bank staff members identify suspicious activity through routine operations. This includes back-office reconciliation identifying discrepancies, tellers observing unusual transaction requests, or other internal observations.

name: Law Enforcement Fraud Referral
description: Detection step initiated through law enforcement agencies reporting compromised accounts or conducting investigations. Sources include police reports, federal agency investigations (FBI, OFAC), and international law enforcement inquiries.

name: Fraud Detection Engine
description: Automated system responsible for monitoring transactions and flagging suspicious activity with a 97%+ detection rate. The FDE operates continuously to identify anomalies and trigger investigation workflows.
context: Fraud Detection Engine (FDE) flags transaction (97%+ detection rate)

name: Customer
description: Customer who reports unauthorized transactions or suspicious account activity. Customers serve as a fraud detection source by proactively contacting the bank about disputed charges or unauthorized activity.
context: Customer calls: 'I didn't authorize this transaction'

name: Bank Staff
description: Bank employees who identify suspicious activity during routine operations. This includes tellers observing unusual transaction requests and back-office staff identifying discrepancies during reconciliation.

name: Law Enforcement Agency
description: External law enforcement agencies that report compromised accounts or conduct investigations. Sources include police departments, federal agencies (FBI, OFAC), and international law enforcement bodies.

name: Fraud Alert
description: Alert generated by the Fraud Detection Engine when suspicious transaction patterns are identified. The alert triggers investigation and intake procedures to assess and respond to potential fraudulent activity.
context: Fraud Detection Engine (FDE) flags transaction (97%+ detection rate)

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: A transaction that was not authorized by the account holder and is reported as fraudulent. These transactions are the subject of fraud detection and investigation across all four discovery channels.
context: Customer calls: 'I didn't authorize this transaction'

name: Fraud Intake Process
description: End-to-end procedure for receiving, triaging, and initiating response to fraud allegations. Begins with formal fraud report submission and includes urgency classification to determine investigation timeline and immediate account security actions.

name: Fraud Report Submission
description: Formal capture of fraud allegation details using standardized Fraud Report Form. Collects reporter identity and category, customer and account information, transaction details, alleged fraudster description, fraud type classification, loss amount, and urgency level.
context: Reporter Category: [Customer / Staff / System / Law Enforcement]

name: Fraud Urgency Triage
description: Classification of fraud report as Urgent or Routine based on threat indicators. Urgent cases require action within 1 hour and include account takeover in progress, large amounts in immediate danger, or law enforcement involvement. Routine cases proceed within 24 hours.

name: Account Security Lockdown
description: Immediate protective actions executed within first 5 minutes of urgent fraud cases to prevent further unauthorized activity. Includes account freeze, card blocking, password reset, session termination, action documentation, customer notification, and escalation trigger for high-value cases.
context: Block customer's debit/credit cards (prevent further fraud)

name: Fraud Urgency Gate
description: Binary decision point determining investigation timeline and response intensity. YES path triggers immediate 1-hour response with account security lockdown. NO path routes to standard 24-hour investigation.

name: High-Value Fraud Escalation Trigger
description: Escalation gate triggered when alleged fraud loss exceeds £5,000 threshold. Cases meeting this threshold are escalated to Financial Crime Head for senior oversight.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime Head if >£5,000

name: Fraud Report Submitter
description: Any party initiating a fraud report, including customers, bank staff, automated systems, or law enforcement. Captured with name, department, and contact phone in the Fraud Report Form.
context: Reporter Category: [Customer / Staff / System / Law Enforcement]

name: Fraud Triage Analyst
description: Operations staff member responsible for executing Initial Triage step, classifying fraud reports as Urgent or Routine based on defined threat indicators.

name: Account Security Response Team
description: Operations team executing immediate account security actions in urgent fraud cases, including account freeze, card blocking, password reset, session termination, and customer notification within the first 5 minutes.
context: Block customer's debit/credit cards (prevent further fraud)

name: Financial Crime Head
description: Senior leadership role responsible for escalation and oversight of high-value fraud cases exceeding £5,000 threshold.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime Head if >£5,000

name: Fraud Allegation
description: Formal fraud allegation received through standardized intake process. Assigned unique Fraud ID with date and sequence number. Triggers triage, investigation, and potential account security response based on urgency classification.
context: Fraud Type: [Account Takeover / Unauthorized Transaction / Other]

name: Account Takeover Fraud
description: Fraud type classification indicating unauthorized access and control of customer account. Classified as urgent trigger requiring immediate 1-hour response and account security lockdown.
context: Fraud Type: [Account Takeover / Unauthorized Transaction / Other]

name: Unauthorized Transaction Fraud
description: Fraud type classification indicating unauthorized transaction(s) on customer account. May be classified as Routine if transaction already posted and no immediate threat exists.
context: Fraud Type: [Account Takeover / Unauthorized Transaction / Other]

name: Customer Account
description: Customer account subject to fraud allegation. Identified by account number in format ACC-XXXXX. May be frozen and have associated cards blocked during urgent fraud response.

name: Customer Debit Card
description: Debit card associated with customer account. Blocked immediately in urgent fraud cases to prevent further unauthorized transactions.
context: Block customer's debit/credit cards (prevent further fraud)

name: Customer Credit Card
description: Credit card associated with customer account. Blocked immediately in urgent fraud cases to prevent further unauthorized transactions.
context: Block customer's debit/credit cards (prevent further fraud)

name: Fraud Allegation Customer
description: Individual customer whose account is subject to fraud allegation. Receives notification by phone during urgent fraud response and has account security actions taken on their behalf.

name: Disputed Transaction
description: Financial transaction(s) alleged to be fraudulent. Captured with transaction date and amount in fraud report. May already be posted to account or represent imminent threat depending on urgency classification.
context: Transaction(s) in Question: [List with dates, amounts]

name: Fraud Investigation Procedure
description: A structured procedure for investigating fraud cases, beginning with systematic evidence preservation. The process requires collection and secure storage of transaction records, account statements, communications, system logs, device information, geo-location data, and written statements. All evidence must be retained for a minimum of 7 years in locked physical or encrypted digital storage, with access restricted to the investigation team.
context: Preserve All Evidence: Required: - [ ] Original transaction records (screenshots, system data) - [ ] Account statements (30 days before fraud date)
Storage: - All evidence secured in locked file (physical) or encrypted (digital) - Separate from normal account files - Access limited to investigation team

name: Evidence Preservation
description: The initial step of the fraud investigation procedure focused on collecting and securing all relevant evidence. This step requires gathering original transaction records, account statements from 30 days prior to the fraud date, all customer and staff communications, system logs with login history and IP addresses, device information, geo-location data, and written statements.
context: Preserve All Evidence: Required: - [ ] Original transaction records (screenshots, system data) - [ ] Account statements (30 days before fraud date) - [ ] All communications (customer emails, phone notes) - [ ] System logs (login history, IP addresses, timestamps)
- [ ] Device information (if known: phone, computer used) - [ ] Geo-location data (where transaction originated) - [ ] Any written statements (customer, staff)

name: Investigation Team
description: The designated team responsible for conducting fraud investigations and maintaining exclusive access to preserved evidence. The investigation team has restricted access to secured evidence files and is responsible for ensuring evidence integrity throughout the investigation process.
context: All evidence secured in locked file (physical) or encrypted (digital) - Separate from normal account files - Access limited to investigation team

name: Fraud Investigation Evidence Collection
description: The systematic collection and preservation of evidence in response to a fraud alert or suspected fraudulent activity. The process encompasses gathering transaction records, account statements, communications, system logs, device information, geo-location data, and written statements, with mandatory secure storage and 7-year retention.
context: Preserve All Evidence: Required: - [ ] Original transaction records (screenshots, system data) - [ ] Account statements (30 days before fraud date)
Storage: - All evidence secured in locked file (physical) or encrypted (digital) - Separate from normal account files - Access limited to investigation team - Not deleted, edited, or altered

name: Original Transaction Records
description: The original transaction records that form the basis of fraud investigation, including screenshots and system data. These records must be preserved as evidence and retained for a minimum of 7 years.
context: - All evidence secured in locked file (physical) or encrypted (digital) - Separate from normal account files - Access limited to investigation team - Not deleted, edited, or altered

name: Account Statement
description: Account statements covering the 30-day period prior to the fraud date, required as evidence in fraud investigations. These statements must be preserved and securely stored as part of the investigation evidence collection.
context: - [ ] Account statements (30 days before fraud date)
Storage: - All evidence secured in locked file (physical) or encrypted (digital) - Separate from normal account files

name: Transaction Analysis Process
description: A systematic procedure for analyzing disputed or flagged transactions to assess legitimacy and detect fraud indicators. The process captures transaction details, evaluates consistency with customer patterns, and identifies red flags including velocity, timing anomalies, high-risk merchants, and geo-impossibilities.

name: Transaction Details Collection
description: Collects and records comprehensive transaction metadata including transaction ID, exact timestamp, amount, transaction type, merchant/recipient information, merchant category, device used, IP address for digital transactions, and geo-location data.

name: Transaction Legitimacy Assessment
description: Evaluates whether a transaction aligns with the customer's known behavior and patterns by assessing amount typicality, merchant familiarity, timing consistency, device novelty, and geo-location deviation from normal activity.
context: - Is amount typical for customer? ☐ Yes ☐ No ☐ Unusual
- Is merchant typical for customer? ☐ Yes ☐ No ☐ Unusual
- Is timing consistent with known patterns? ☐ Yes ☐ No

name: Red Flag Identification
description: Identifies and flags specific fraud indicators and suspicious patterns including transaction velocity, unusual timing (3 AM transactions), high-risk merchant categories, geo-impossibilities, and deviations from habitual customer behavior.

name: Amount Typicality Decision
description: Determines whether the transaction amount is typical, unusual, or atypical for the customer's normal spending patterns. Outcomes inform risk scoring and escalation decisions.
context: - Is amount typical for customer? ☐ Yes ☐ No ☐ Unusual

name: Merchant Typicality Decision
description: Assesses whether the merchant or recipient is typical for the customer or represents an unusual or new transaction partner. Flags deviations from habitual patterns.
context: - Is merchant typical for customer? ☐ Yes ☐ No ☐ Unusual
- Change from habitual pattern (customer never transfers to this recipient)

name: Timing Consistency Decision
description: Evaluates whether the transaction timing aligns with the customer's known activity patterns. Flags transactions at unusual hours (e.g., 3 AM) or inconsistent with historical behavior.
context: - Is timing consistent with known patterns? ☐ Yes ☐ No

name: Device Novelty Decision
description: Determines whether the device used for the transaction is new or unusual compared to the customer's typical transaction methods.

name: Geo-location Deviation Decision
description: Assesses whether the transaction geo-location differs from the customer's normal activity area or represents a geo-impossibility (multiple transactions in geographically distant locations within an impossible timeframe).
context: - Is geo-location different from normal? ☐ Yes ☐ No ☐ Impossible
- ☐ Geo-impossibility (2 transactions on opposite sides of world within minutes)

name: Velocity Check Decision
description: Flags transactions occurring in rapid succession (multiple transactions in short time), a common indicator of account compromise or fraudulent activity.

name: High-Risk Merchant Category Decision
description: Identifies transactions with high-risk merchant categories including casinos, money transfer services, and other categories associated with fraud or money laundering.

name: Disputed Transaction
description: A financial transaction on a customer account that has been flagged as potentially fraudulent or disputed, requiring detailed analysis of transaction details, legitimacy assessment, and red flag evaluation.

name: Fraud Investigation
description: The systematic investigation of disputed or flagged transactions to determine fraud likelihood through pattern analysis, red flag identification, and legitimacy assessment.

name: Customer Interview Procedure
description: A structured interview process conducted within 24 hours of a fraud report to distinguish between legitimate customer activities and fraudulent transactions. The procedure covers authentication, account access, device security, communications, merchant verification, and timeline reconstruction through a standardized questionnaire.
context: Timing: Within 24 hours of report (unless law enforcement requests delay)
Scope: Understanding customer's legitimate activities vs. fraudulent
Customer statement taken (audio recorded if possible)

name: Authentication and Authorization Verification
description: Initial questioning phase to establish whether the customer authorized the disputed transaction and to understand their relationship with the transaction recipient.
context: Did you authorize this transaction of £[amount] on [date]?
Would you ever send money to a stranger/unknown entity?

name: Account Access Assessment
description: Questioning phase to determine how the customer's account may have been compromised, including card storage practices, recent card usage, password change history, and PIN/password sharing.
context: Where are your cards normally kept?
When did you last use your card in person?
When did you last change your online banking password?
Do you share your PIN/password with anyone?

name: Device Security Evaluation
description: Questioning phase to identify potential device compromise vectors, including unusual app downloads, device loss or theft, and device usage patterns for online banking.
context: Do you use the same device (phone/computer) for online banking?
Have you downloaded unusual apps recently?
Has your device been lost or stolen?

name: Communication Threat Assessment
description: Questioning phase to identify phishing, social engineering, or other communication-based fraud vectors, including suspicious emails, unsolicited calls, and pre-transaction contact.
context: Have you received suspicious emails requesting information?
Have you received calls asking for account details?
Did anyone contact you before this transaction?

name: Merchant and Recipient Verification
description: Questioning phase to establish customer familiarity with the transaction recipient or merchant, prior business relationship, and whether the customer initiated or received contact.
context: Have you done business with them before?
Did you initiate contact, or did they contact you?

name: Timeline Reconstruction
description: Questioning phase requiring the customer to walk through their activities on the transaction date, establish their location during the transaction, and identify when they first discovered the unauthorized activity.
context: Walk me through your day on [date].
Where were you when this transaction occurred?
When did you first notice the unauthorized transaction?

name: Interview Documentation and Recording
description: Final step to formally record interview completion, interviewer identity, interview method, customer statement capture, and customer confirmation or dispute of facts.
context: Customer statement taken (audio recorded if possible)

name: Fraud Investigation Interviewer
description: The staff member responsible for conducting the customer interview within 24 hours of a fraud report, asking standardized questions across six topic areas, and documenting the customer's responses.
context: Customer statement taken (audio recorded if possible)

name: Customer Under Fraud Investigation
description: The account holder being interviewed regarding a disputed or fraudulent transaction, providing information about authorization, account access, device security, communications, and transaction timeline.
context: Understanding customer's legitimate activities vs. fraudulent

name: Transaction Authorization Confirmation
description: Decision gate determining whether the customer authorized the disputed transaction. The outcome branches investigation toward either legitimate activity or confirmed fraud.
context: Did you authorize this transaction of £[amount] on [date]?

name: Account Compromise Vector Identification
description: Decision gate determining whether the customer's account was compromised through card theft, password compromise, or unauthorized access. Outcome determines investigation focus and remediation steps.
context: Where are your cards normally kept?
When did you last change your online banking password?
Do you share your PIN/password with anyone?

name: Device Compromise Assessment
description: Decision gate determining whether the customer's device was compromised through malware, unusual apps, or physical theft. Outcome informs fraud investigation direction and customer remediation advice.
context: Do you use the same device (phone/computer) for online banking?
Have you downloaded unusual apps recently?
Has your device been lost or stolen?

name: Social Engineering or Phishing Detection
description: Decision gate determining whether the customer was targeted by phishing emails, social engineering calls, or other communication-based fraud vectors. Outcome escalates investigation and informs customer protection measures.
context: Have you received suspicious emails requesting information?
Have you received calls asking for account details?
Did anyone contact you before this transaction?

name: Merchant Familiarity and Legitimacy Assessment
description: Decision gate determining whether the customer recognizes the transaction recipient or merchant and has prior business relationship. Outcome distinguishes between known merchant transactions and unknown/suspicious recipients.
context: Have you done business with them before?
Did you initiate contact, or did they contact you?

name: Timeline Consistency Verification
description: Decision gate determining whether the customer's account of their location and activities on the transaction date is consistent with the transaction details. Outcome validates or contradicts the fraud claim.
context: Walk me through your day on [date].
Where were you when this transaction occurred?
When did you first notice the unauthorized transaction?

name: Fraud Investigation Interview
description: A structured investigation response to a fraud report involving direct customer contact within 24 hours to gather evidence, establish authorization status, identify compromise vectors, and document findings for fraud determination.
context: Timing: Within 24 hours of report (unless law enforcement requests delay)
Scope: Understanding customer's legitimate activities vs. fraudulent

name: Disputed Transaction Under Investigation
description: A financial transaction on the customer's account that is disputed as unauthorized or fraudulent, subject to investigation through the customer interview procedure to determine legitimacy and establish fraud liability.
context: Did you authorize this transaction of £[amount] on [date]?
When did you first notice the unauthorized transaction?

name: Fraud Evidence Evaluation Process
description: A structured procedure for evaluating fraud likelihood by scoring multiple pieces of evidence across six dimensions: customer dispute strength, geographic impossibility, device mismatch, merchant risk, transaction velocity, and customer history. The process produces a cumulative fraud score (0–12) that determines whether the claim is confirmed fraud, likely fraud, possible fraud, unlikely fraud, or not fraud, with corresponding actions for each outcome.
context: Assess Fraud Likelihood: For Each Piece of Evidence, Score
Fraud Score = Sum of Evidence Points (0–12)

name: Customer Dispute Claim Assessment
description: Evaluation of the customer's dispute claim strength, scored on a scale of 1–3 where 1 indicates a weak claim and 3 indicates a strong claim backed by facts.
context: Customer Disputes Transaction | 1–3 | 1=Weak claim, 3=Strong claim (backed by facts)

name: Geographic Impossibility Check
description: Assessment of whether the transaction location is geographically impossible relative to the customer's known location or recent activity, scored 0–2 where 2 indicates confirmed impossibility and 0 indicates the transaction is possible.

name: Device Mismatch Evaluation
description: Determination of whether the transaction was initiated from a device different from those known to be used by the customer, scored 0–2 where 2 indicates a new device and 0 indicates a known device.

name: Merchant Risk Classification
description: Classification of the merchant involved in the transaction by risk level, scored 0–2 where 2 indicates a high-risk merchant and 0 indicates a legitimate merchant.

name: Transaction Velocity Analysis
description: Analysis of the frequency and timing of transactions, scored 0–2 where 2 indicates multiple rapid transactions and 0 indicates a single transaction.

name: Customer History Pattern Review
description: Review of the customer's transaction history and behavioral patterns to determine whether the disputed transaction is typical or atypical, scored 0–2 where 2 indicates the customer never performs such transactions and 0 indicates the transaction is typical.

name: Fraud Score Calculation
description: Summation of all evidence points across the six assessment dimensions to produce a cumulative fraud score ranging from 0 to 12.
context: Fraud Score = Sum of Evidence Points (0–12)

name: Fraud Score Outcome Gate
description: A branching decision point that routes the fraud case to different outcomes based on the cumulative fraud score: scores 10–12 trigger refund and investigation (fraud confirmed); 7–9 trigger refund and investigation (fraud likely); 4–6 trigger investigation or conditional refund (fraud possible); 1–3 result in customer education (fraud unlikely); 0 results in claim denial and customer education (fraud not likely).
context: 4–6 | Fraud Possible | Investigate further or refund pending
1–3 | Fraud Unlikely | Likely authorized or error; educate customer
0 | Fraud Not Likely | Deny fraud claim; educate customer

name: Fraud Investigation Trigger
description: An investigation process initiated when fraud evidence evaluation produces a score of 7 or higher, indicating fraud is likely or confirmed. The investigation is accompanied by customer refund authorization.

name: Fraud Possible Further Investigation
description: An investigation or conditional refund process initiated when fraud evidence evaluation produces a score of 4–6, indicating fraud is possible but not confirmed. The outcome determines whether a refund is issued pending investigation completion.
context: 4–6 | Fraud Possible | Investigate further or refund pending

name: Customer Education on Fraud Unlikely
description: A customer communication action taken when fraud evidence evaluation produces a score of 1–3, indicating fraud is unlikely. The customer is educated that the transaction is likely authorized or an error rather than fraudulent.
context: 1–3 | Fraud Unlikely | Likely authorized or error; educate customer

name: Fraud Claim Denial with Customer Education
description: A claim denial action taken when fraud evidence evaluation produces a score of 0, indicating fraud is not likely. The customer is denied the fraud claim and educated on the assessment outcome.
context: 0 | Fraud Not Likely | Deny fraud claim; educate customer

name: Disputed Transaction
description: A financial transaction on a customer account that the customer has disputed as fraudulent or unauthorized. The transaction is the subject of the fraud evidence evaluation process and is scored across multiple fraud indicators.
context: Assess Fraud Likelihood: For Each Piece of Evidence, Score

name: Merchant/Third-Party Investigation
description: A fraud investigation step triggered when fraudulent activity involves an external merchant or third-party recipient. The step branches into two paths: card transaction investigation (merchant contact, proof of presence, receipt/footage review, chargeback history) and transfer investigation (recipient bank identification, account verification, sanctions screening, fund recovery tracking).
context: Track recipient account (is it in sanctions list? Multiple fraud reports?)

name: Card Transaction Merchant Contact
description: A sub-step within merchant investigation specific to card transactions. Involves contacting the merchant to obtain transaction proof, evidence of customer presence (for card-present transactions), and merchant records including receipts and camera footage.
context: Request proof customer was present (if card-present)

name: Merchant Chargeback History Review
description: An investigation step that reviews the merchant's chargeback history to identify whether the merchant is a repeat offender in fraud cases, informing the fraud assessment and recovery strategy.
context: Review merchant chargeback history (are they repeat offender?)

name: External Account Transfer Investigation
description: A sub-step within merchant investigation specific to transfers to external accounts. Involves identifying the recipient bank, requesting transaction details, verifying recipient name matches the account, screening the recipient account against sanctions lists, and checking for multiple fraud reports.
context: Request transaction details (recipient name matches account?)
Track recipient account (is it in sanctions list? Multiple fraud reports?)

name: Recipient Account Sanctions Screening
description: A compliance check within transfer investigation that screens the recipient account against sanctions lists to determine if the account is linked to sanctioned entities or high-risk parties.
context: Track recipient account (is it in sanctions list? Multiple fraud reports?)

name: Fund Recovery Attempt
description: An urgent investigation step executed when fraudulent funds remain in the recipient account. Involves immediate contact with the recipient bank to attempt recovery of the transferred funds.
context: If funds still in recipient account: Attempt to recover (urgent)

name: Withdrawal Location Tracing
description: An investigation step executed when fraudulent funds have already been withdrawn from the recipient account. Involves tracing the withdrawal location and escalating to law enforcement for further investigation.
context: If funds withdrawn: Trace withdrawal location (law enforcement)

name: Fraud Involves External Merchant or Third Party
description: A branching decision point that determines whether the fraud involves an external merchant or third-party recipient, triggering the Merchant/Third-Party Investigation process. If yes, the investigation branches into card transaction or transfer-specific paths.

name: Funds Status in Recipient Account
description: A critical decision point that determines whether fraudulent funds remain in the recipient account or have been withdrawn. If funds remain, urgent recovery is attempted; if withdrawn, the case is escalated to law enforcement for withdrawal location tracing.
context: If funds still in recipient account: Attempt to recover (urgent)
If funds withdrawn: Trace withdrawal location (law enforcement)

name: External Merchant Fraud Event
description: A fraud investigation triggered by fraudulent activity involving an external merchant or third-party recipient. The investigation encompasses merchant contact, proof verification, chargeback history review, and fund recovery or law enforcement escalation depending on fund status.

name: Sanctions Screening for Recipient Account
description: A mandatory compliance gate that screens the recipient account against sanctions lists during fraud investigation of external transfers. Verifies whether the recipient account is linked to sanctioned entities or has multiple fraud reports.
context: Track recipient account (is it in sanctions list? Multiple fraud reports?)

name: Fraud Investigation Team
description: The operational role responsible for executing merchant/third-party fraud investigations, including contacting merchants, requesting documentation, reviewing chargeback history, identifying recipient banks, and coordinating fund recovery or law enforcement escalation.

name: Merchant Contact Point
description: The external merchant entity responsible for providing transaction proof, evidence of customer presence, receipts, camera footage, and chargeback history information during fraud investigation.
context: Request proof customer was present (if card-present)

name: Recipient Bank
description: The external financial institution holding the recipient account. Responsible for providing transaction details, verifying recipient account information, and cooperating with fund recovery attempts when fraudulent transfers are identified.
context: Request transaction details (recipient name matches account?)

name: Law Enforcement
description: External law enforcement authority engaged when fraudulent funds have been withdrawn from the recipient account. Responsible for tracing withdrawal locations and pursuing criminal investigation.

name: Debit Card
description: A payment card referenced in the fraud investigation process for card-present and card-not-present transactions. Fraud investigation for card transactions includes merchant contact, proof of presence verification, and receipt/footage review.
context: Request proof customer was present (if card-present)

name: Card Transaction
description: A financial transaction conducted via card at an external merchant that is subject to fraud investigation. Investigation includes merchant contact for transaction proof and verification of customer presence.
context: Request proof customer was present (if card-present)

name: External Account Transfer
description: A financial transfer to an external account that is subject to fraud investigation. Investigation includes recipient bank identification, account verification, sanctions screening, and fund recovery or law enforcement escalation based on fund status.
context: Track recipient account (is it in sanctions list? Multiple fraud reports?)

name: Forensic Investigation Process
description: A specialized investigation procedure triggered for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime cases. The process involves forensic analysis across multiple domains (email, device, network, financial, and database) and is managed by the Head of Financial Crime with engagement of external or internal forensics teams. Estimated timeline is 2–4 weeks with costs ranging from £5k–£20k depending on complexity.
context: For High-Loss Fraud or Suspected Cybercrime
Case file transferred to external/internal forensics team

name: Email Header Analysis
description: A forensic analysis step that traces phishing emails to identify their origin and authenticity. This step is part of the broader forensic investigation for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime.

name: Device Forensics
description: A forensic analysis step examining customer devices when they are involved in a fraud incident. This step is part of the broader forensic investigation for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime.

name: Network Forensics
description: A forensic analysis step that examines IP logs and may involve ISP subpoenas to trace network activity related to fraud. This step is part of the broader forensic investigation for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime.

name: Financial Forensics
description: A forensic analysis step that traces the flow of money to identify where fraudulently obtained funds have been transferred or spent. This step is part of the broader forensic investigation for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime.

name: Database Queries
description: A forensic analysis step that queries internal databases to identify linked frauds and patterns across multiple victims or incidents. This step is part of the broader forensic investigation for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime.

name: Forensic Investigator Engagement Request
description: The step in which a request is made to the Head of Financial Crime to engage forensic investigators for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime cases. This initiates the transfer of the case file to external or internal forensics teams.
context: Request made to Head of Financial Crime
Case file transferred to external/internal forensics team

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: The senior role responsible for receiving forensic investigation requests and authorizing the engagement of external or internal forensics teams for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime cases.
context: Request made to Head of Financial Crime

name: Forensic Investigator
description: The specialized team (external or internal) engaged to conduct forensic analysis across email, device, network, financial, and database domains for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime cases.
context: Case file transferred to external/internal forensics team

name: High-Loss Fraud Investigation
description: A fraud alert classification for high-loss or complex fraud incidents that triggers engagement of forensic investigators. The investigation aims to identify the fraudster, fraud patterns, entry points, and prevention recommendations.
context: For High-Loss Fraud or Suspected Cybercrime
Findings May Reveal: Identity of fraudster (if traceable), Fraud pattern (linked to other victims), Entry point (how fraud occurred), Recommendations for prevention

name: Suspected Cybercrime Investigation
description: A fraud alert classification for suspected cybercrime incidents that triggers engagement of forensic investigators. The investigation may involve device forensics, network forensics, and financial tracing to identify the perpetrator and prevent future incidents.
context: For High-Loss Fraud or Suspected Cybercrime

name: Fraud Investigation Process
description: An end-to-end procedure for investigating suspected fraud or disputed transactions. The process culminates in a formal determination of the transaction's status based on gathered evidence, with outcomes categorized as confirmed fraud, disputed transaction, authorized transaction, customer error, or incomplete investigation.
context: DISPUTED TRANSACTION — Ambiguous, but balance of evidence favors customer

name: Investigation Conclusion
description: The final step in the fraud investigation process where all gathered evidence is reviewed and a formal determination is made regarding the nature and status of the disputed or suspected fraudulent transaction.

name: Fraud Determination Gate
description: A multi-path decision gate that classifies the investigation outcome into one of five categories: confirmed fraud, disputed transaction, authorized transaction, customer error, or incomplete investigation. Each path triggers different resolution and notification actions.
context: ☐ DISPUTED TRANSACTION — Ambiguous, but balance of evidence favors customer
☐ CUSTOMER ERROR — System worked correctly; customer misunderstood
☐ INCOMPLETE — Insufficient evidence; close with follow-up conditions

name: Confirmed Fraud Determination
description: A determination outcome indicating that the transaction was confirmed as fraudulent, perpetrated by an unauthorized third party rather than the account holder.

name: Disputed Transaction Determination
description: A determination outcome indicating that the transaction status is ambiguous or unclear, but the balance of available evidence favors the customer's claim of unauthorized or erroneous activity.
context: ☐ DISPUTED TRANSACTION — Ambiguous, but balance of evidence favors customer

name: Authorized Transaction Determination
description: A determination outcome indicating that the transaction was authorized by the customer, who now regrets the transaction but has no grounds for a fraud or dispute claim.

name: Customer Error Determination
description: A determination outcome indicating that the banking system operated correctly and the transaction was processed as intended; the customer's complaint stems from misunderstanding rather than system failure or fraud.
context: ☐ CUSTOMER ERROR — System worked correctly; customer misunderstood

name: Incomplete Investigation Determination
description: A determination outcome indicating that insufficient evidence has been gathered to reach a conclusive determination. The investigation is closed with follow-up conditions or additional evidence requirements.
context: ☐ INCOMPLETE — Insufficient evidence; close with follow-up conditions

name: Fraud Resolution Process
description: End-to-end procedure for resolving fraud cases by type, determining refund eligibility, and implementing prevention actions. The process branches on fraud confirmation status and includes refund calculation with interest, customer notification, and account protection measures.

name: Issue Full Refund to Customer Account
description: First step in the confirmed fraud refund process where the full transaction amount is credited back to the customer's account.
context: Issue full refund to customer account

name: Calculate and Include Interest on Refund
description: Calculation step that determines interest accrued on the refunded amount using daily rate multiplied by the number of days between transaction posting and refund decision.
context: Refund includes interest (daily rate × days delayed)
Interest Accrued: £1,000 × 0.05% annual rate ÷ 365 days × 2 days = £0.27

name: Timestamp Refund Decision
description: Recording step that documents the date and time when the refund decision is made for audit and compliance purposes.

name: Process Refund Within 10 Business Days
description: Execution step that ensures the refund is posted to the customer account within the 10 business day timeline mandated by the Direct Debit Guarantee.
context: Process within 10 business days (Direct Debit Guarantee)

name: Notify Customer in Writing
description: Communication step that informs the customer in writing of the refund decision, amount, and posting date.

name: Issue New Card
description: Prevention action step that replaces the compromised card with a new one to prevent further unauthorized use.

name: Reset Online Banking Password
description: Prevention action step that resets the customer's online banking credentials to prevent account takeover.

name: Enable Two-Factor Authentication
description: Prevention action step that activates two-factor authentication on the customer account if not already in place.

name: Flag Account for Enhanced Monitoring
description: Prevention action step that marks the account for heightened transaction monitoring following a confirmed fraud incident.

name: Review Standing Orders and Direct Debits
description: Prevention action step that audits all standing orders and direct debits on the account to identify any unauthorized payment instructions that may have been set up by the fraudster.
context: Review standing orders / direct debits (may be compromised)

name: Offer Identity Theft Protection
description: Prevention action step that provides identity theft protection services to the customer in cases where account takeover is suspected.
context: Offer identity theft protection (if account takeover)

name: Educate Customer on Fraud Occurrence
description: Prevention action step that explains to the customer how the fraud occurred and what security measures they should take.
context: Educate customer on how fraud occurred

name: Assess Balance of Evidence for Disputed Transaction
description: Investigation step that evaluates available evidence to determine whether a disputed transaction should be refunded, partially refunded, or rejected.
context: If Balance of Evidence Favors Customer

name: Offer Partial Refund for Inconclusive Cases
description: Step for disputed transactions where evidence is inconclusive, offering a partial refund (e.g., 50%) pending additional verification.

name: Follow Up on Disputed Transaction in 30 Days
description: Follow-up step that re-engages with the customer 30 days after a partial refund to gather additional evidence or resolve the dispute.

name: Explain Authorized Transaction Status
description: Communication step that clarifies to the customer that the transaction was authorized by them and therefore not subject to fraud refund.
context: Explain transaction was authorized by customer

name: Offer Chargeback Process
description: Step that informs the customer of the chargeback process as an alternative remedy for disputes with merchants rather than the bank.

name: Educate Customer on Regrettable Purchases
description: Education step that advises the customer on how to prevent future regrettable purchases through better decision-making practices.
context: Educate on how to prevent future regrettable purchases

name: Explain Customer Error and System Correctness
description: Communication step that clarifies to the customer that no fraud occurred and that the system operated correctly, with the error being customer misunderstanding.

name: Educate Customer on Banking Protections
description: Education step that informs the customer about relevant banking protections such as Direct Debit Guarantee or Standing Order mechanics.
context: Educate customer (e.g., "Direct Debit Guarantee protection", "Standing Order", etc.)

name: Document Customer Education in File
description: Recording step that logs the customer education provided in the customer file for future reference and pattern analysis.
context: Document in customer file (pattern of similar disputes?)

name: Fraud Type Classification Decision
description: Primary branching decision that categorizes the case into one of four paths: confirmed fraud, disputed transaction, authorized but regretted, or customer error. Each path triggers different resolution procedures.

name: Disputed Transaction Evidence Assessment
description: Secondary decision point for disputed transactions that branches based on the balance of evidence: favors customer (full refund), inconclusive (partial refund with follow-up), or favors merchant (no refund).
context: If Balance of Evidence Favors Customer

name: Fraud Resolution Officer
description: The operational role responsible for executing the fraud resolution process, including refund calculations, decision timestamping, and customer notifications.
context: Issue full refund to customer account

name: Fraud Investigation Team
description: The team responsible for investigating disputed transactions, assessing evidence balance, and determining fraud classification.
context: If Balance of Evidence Favors Customer

name: Customer Service Representative
description: The role responsible for customer-facing communications including notifications, education, and follow-up on fraud cases.
context: Educate customer on how fraud occurred
Educate on how to prevent future regrettable purchases

name: Account Security Team
description: The team responsible for implementing prevention actions including card issuance, password resets, 2FA activation, and account monitoring flags.

name: Direct Debit Guarantee Compliance
description: Mandatory compliance gate ensuring refunds are processed within the 10 business day timeline required by the Direct Debit Guarantee scheme.
context: Process within 10 business days (Direct Debit Guarantee)

name: Fraudulent Transaction Jan 5 £1,000
description: Example fraudulent transaction of £1,000 posted on January 5 used to illustrate refund calculation including interest accrual.
context: Refund Decision Date: Jan 7 (2 days later)
Interest Accrued: £1,000 × 0.05% annual rate ÷ 365 days × 2 days = £0.27

name: Compromised Debit Card
description: The customer's debit card that has been compromised through fraud and requires replacement as part of the prevention actions.

name: Direct Debit Mandate
description: Direct debit mandates on the customer account that may have been compromised by fraudsters and require review as part of fraud prevention.
context: Review standing orders / direct debits (may be compromised)

name: Standing Order
description: Standing order payment instructions on the customer account that may have been compromised by fraudsters and require review as part of fraud prevention.
context: Review standing orders / direct debits (may be compromised)

name: Fraud Investigation
description: The fraud investigation process triggered by a customer dispute or fraud detection, leading to classification and resolution according to the fraud type.

name: Customer
description: The individual customer whose account is subject to fraud investigation and who receives refunds, notifications, and education as part of the resolution process.
context: Issue full refund to customer account
Educate customer on how fraud occurred

name: Fraud Classification and Reporting
description: A discrete operational step that classifies detected fraud incidents by type, amount, and recovery status, then routes them to appropriate internal and regulatory reporting channels based on money laundering or sanctions evasion indicators.
context: Classify Fraud for Reporting: Type: [Account Takeover / Card Fraud / Check Fraud / Impersonation / Other]
Status: [Resolved / Under Investigation / Referred to Police]

name: Fraud Confirmation Gate
description: A branching decision point that determines whether fraud has been confirmed (Yes/No), which affects the classification record and downstream reporting obligations.

name: SAR Filing Trigger
description: A regulatory gate that determines whether a Suspicious Activity Report must be filed based on whether the fraud involves suspected money laundering or sanctions evasion.
context: File if fraud suspected involving money laundering/sanctions evasion
Example: Customer transfers funds to sanctions country

name: Data Breach Applicability Check
description: A decision point that determines whether customer data has been compromised, triggering mandatory data breach reporting to the FCA and customer notification.
context: Data Breach Report (If Applicable): File if customer data compromised

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: The senior role responsible for receiving and reviewing the monthly Financial Crime Report summarizing fraud cases, trends, and prevention effectiveness.
context: Submitted monthly to Head of Financial Crime

name: Fraud Investigation Team
description: The operational team responsible for classifying fraud incidents by type, amount, and recovery status, and determining whether regulatory reporting is required.
context: Fraud Classification: Type: [Account Takeover / Card Fraud / Check Fraud / Impersonation / Other]
Status: [Resolved / Under Investigation / Referred to Police]

name: FCA Reporting Authority
description: The external regulatory authority that receives Suspicious Activity Reports within 30 days and data breach notifications within 72 hours.

name: SAR Filing Obligation
description: A mandatory regulatory gate requiring the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report with the FCA within 30 days when fraud involves suspected money laundering or sanctions evasion.
context: Suspicious Activity Report (SAR): File if fraud suspected involving money laundering/sanctions evasion

name: Data Breach Notification Compliance
description: A mandatory regulatory gate requiring notification to the FCA within 72 hours and immediate customer notification when customer data is compromised.
context: Data Breach Report (If Applicable): File if customer data compromised

name: Account Takeover Fraud
description: A fraud classification category representing unauthorized access and control of a customer account by a third party.
context: Type: [Account Takeover / Card Fraud / Check Fraud / Impersonation / Other]

name: Card Fraud Event
description: A fraud classification category representing unauthorized use or compromise of a payment card.
context: Type: [Account Takeover / Card Fraud / Check Fraud / Impersonation / Other]

name: Check Fraud Event
description: A fraud classification category representing fraudulent check issuance or alteration.
context: Type: [Account Takeover / Card Fraud / Check Fraud / Impersonation / Other]

name: Impersonation Fraud
description: A fraud classification category representing fraudulent misrepresentation of identity to gain unauthorized access or funds.
context: Type: [Account Takeover / Card Fraud / Check Fraud / Impersonation / Other]

name: SAR Filing Deadline
description: The regulatory deadline requiring Suspicious Activity Reports to be filed with the FCA within 30 days of fraud detection involving suspected money laundering or sanctions evasion.

name: Sanctions Evasion Screening
description: An AML screening control that identifies fraud cases involving transfers to sanctioned jurisdictions or entities, triggering SAR filing obligations.
context: File if fraud suspected involving money laundering/sanctions evasion
Example: Customer transfers funds to sanctions country

name: Money Laundering Detection
description: An AML screening control that identifies fraud cases with suspected money laundering indicators, triggering SAR filing obligations.
context: File if fraud suspected involving money laundering/sanctions evasion

name: Law Enforcement Coordination Process
description: End-to-end procedure for determining when and how to report fraud incidents to law enforcement. Establishes mandatory and optional reporting thresholds based on fraud type, amount, pattern, and customer request.

name: Confirmed Fraud Assessment
description: Evaluation step to determine if fraud has been confirmed and assess whether the amount exceeds £10,000 threshold for mandatory police reporting.

name: Serial Fraud Pattern Detection
description: Analysis step to identify whether fraud involves multiple victims or demonstrates a recognizable pattern indicative of organized or serial fraud activity.

name: Organized Fraud Ring Assessment
description: Investigation step to determine whether the fraud is part of an organized fraud ring operation, triggering mandatory police escalation.

name: Identity Theft and Impersonation Check
description: Verification step to identify cases involving impersonation or identity theft, which mandate police reporting regardless of amount.

name: Check Fraud Coordination
description: Coordination step with bank systems team to verify check fraud incidents and determine police reporting requirement.
context: Check fraud (coordinated with bank systems team)

name: Customer Police Report Request Handling
description: Process step to handle customer requests for police reports, which trigger mandatory reporting regardless of fraud amount or type.

name: High-Value Fraud Reporting Decision
description: Optional reporting decision for fraud exceeding £5,000 threshold, with encouragement to report to police for pattern recognition and prevention.

name: Repeated Fraudster Pattern Recognition
description: Analysis step to identify repeat fraudsters and recognize patterns that may warrant optional police reporting for prevention purposes.

name: Suspected Insider Fraud Escalation
description: Mandatory escalation step for suspected insider fraud cases, which always require police reporting regardless of amount or other factors.

name: Mandatory Police Report Trigger
description: Decision gate determining whether fraud incident meets mandatory reporting criteria (confirmed fraud >£10,000, serial fraud, organized ring, identity theft, check fraud, customer request, or insider fraud).
context: Check fraud (coordinated with bank systems team)

name: Optional Police Report Assessment
description: Decision gate for optional police reporting of fraud between £5,000-£10,000, repeated fraudster patterns, or other discretionary cases where reporting is encouraged but not mandated.

name: Fraud Investigation Team
description: Team responsible for assessing fraud incidents, determining reporting thresholds, and coordinating with law enforcement and bank systems teams.

name: Bank Systems Team
description: Team responsible for coordinating check fraud verification and providing technical assessment to support police reporting decisions.
context: Check fraud (coordinated with bank systems team)

name: Law Enforcement Authority
description: External law enforcement agency receiving mandatory and optional fraud reports from the bank.

name: Confirmed Fraud Event
description: Fraud incident that has been confirmed and assessed for police reporting based on amount, type, pattern, and customer request.

name: Identity Theft Fraud Alert
description: Fraud alert triggered by impersonation or identity theft, mandating immediate police reporting.

name: Check Fraud Alert
description: Fraud alert for check-related fraud incidents requiring coordination with bank systems team and police reporting assessment.
context: Check fraud (coordinated with bank systems team)

name: Insider Fraud Alert
description: Fraud alert for suspected insider fraud, which always mandates police reporting regardless of amount or other factors.

name: Police Report Process
description: End-to-end procedure for reporting suspected fraud to local police, including internal notification, formal police report filing, evidence preservation and coordination, and ongoing follow-up with law enforcement. The process ensures proper documentation and coordination between the bank's financial crime and legal teams and police investigators.

name: Internal Notification
description: Initial step requiring notification of key stakeholders within the bank before filing a police report. Involves notifying the Head of Financial Crime and Head of Legal, and formally documenting the decision to report to police.

name: File Police Report
description: Step involving direct contact with local police to file a formal report. Includes providing case details and evidence, obtaining a police reference number for tracking, and documenting the report in the case file.

name: Evidence Management
description: Step focused on preserving evidence for police investigation and coordinating with law enforcement on account handling and customer communication. Includes refraining from disturbing the suspected fraudster's account to allow police monitoring and providing requested documents and data to police.
context: Don't disturb suspected fraudster's account (police may monitor)
Coordinate with police on customer communication

name: Follow-Up
description: Final step involving ongoing communication with police to track case progress and provide additional evidence as requested. Requires periodic contact with police and comprehensive documentation of all communications.
context: Periodically contact police for case status

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: Senior role responsible for receiving notification of suspected fraud cases before police reporting and participating in the decision to escalate to law enforcement.

name: Head of Legal
description: Senior legal role responsible for receiving notification of suspected fraud cases and advising on the decision to report to police.

name: Local Police
description: External law enforcement authority responsible for receiving fraud reports, investigating cases, and requesting evidence and documentation from the bank. Contact via non-emergency number 101 in UK.
context: Coordinate with police on customer communication
Periodically contact police for case status

name: Fraud Investigation
description: Investigation into suspected fraud activity that triggers the police reporting process. Involves preservation of evidence, coordination with law enforcement, and ongoing case management.
context: Don't disturb suspected fraudster's account (police may monitor)

name: Fraud Investigation Case Documentation and Closure Process
description: End-to-end process for documenting and closing a fraud investigation case. Requires compilation of a complete case file containing intake forms, customer interviews, transaction documentation, evidence, analysis, findings, refund decisions, prevention actions, and management sign-off before case closure.
context: Complete Fraud Investigation Case File Must Contain:

name: Original Fraud Report Collection
description: Initial step in case documentation requiring collection and filing of the original fraud report intake form as part of the complete case file.

name: Customer Interview Documentation
description: Collection and recording of customer interview notes or recordings as evidence within the fraud investigation case file.

name: Transaction Documentation Collection
description: Compilation of transaction documentation including screenshots and statements as supporting evidence in the fraud investigation case file.

name: Evidence Collection and Recording
description: Collection and filing of all evidence including communications and system logs relevant to the fraud investigation.

name: Investigation Analysis and Findings
description: Analytical review and documentation of findings derived from the collected evidence and investigation activities.

name: Investigation Conclusion and Determination
description: Formal conclusion and determination of the fraud investigation findings, establishing whether fraud was confirmed or not.

name: Refund Decision Documentation
description: Documentation of the refund decision made as a result of the fraud investigation, if applicable to the case outcome.

name: Prevention Actions Recording
description: Documentation of prevention actions and measures taken to prevent similar fraud incidents in the future.

name: Police Report Reference Filing
description: Recording and filing of police report reference numbers when applicable to the fraud investigation case.

name: Management Sign-Off and Approval
description: Formal approval and sign-off by manager or Head of Crime authorizing case closure and validating all documentation.

name: Case Closure Recording
description: Recording of the date on which the fraud investigation case is formally closed in the system.

name: Investigation Timeline Documentation
description: Documentation of the complete timeline of the investigation from initial report through case closure.
context: ☐ Timeline of investigation (from report to closure)

name: Manager or Head of Crime
description: Senior role responsible for reviewing, approving, and signing off on completed fraud investigation case files before closure.

name: Fraud Investigation Case File
description: Comprehensive documentation package containing all required elements of a completed fraud investigation, from intake through closure and management approval.
context: Complete Fraud Investigation Case File Must Contain:

name: Fraud Investigation Case Closure Process
description: End-to-end procedure for closing a fraud investigation case once all evidence has been gathered, a determination made, and appropriate remedial actions completed. Includes customer notification, refund issuance, prevention measures, and police reporting where applicable.
context: Investigation Complete When: All evidence gathered and analyzed, Determination made (fraud/not fraud/inconclusive)
Customer refunded (if applicable), Prevention actions implemented, Police report filed (if applicable), Case documented, Manager approval obtained

name: Evidence Gathering and Analysis
description: Initial step in case closure where all available evidence related to the disputed transaction is collected and thoroughly analyzed to support the fraud determination.

name: Fraud Determination
description: Critical decision step where investigators conclude whether the transaction is confirmed fraud, not fraud, or inconclusive based on the evidence analysis.

name: Customer Refund Issuance
description: Step where the disputed transaction amount is refunded to the customer's account when fraud is confirmed. Refund processing includes notification of the refund date and expected clearing time.
context: Refund of £[amount] issued to your account on [date]
Please allow 1–2 business days for the refund to appear

name: Fraud Prevention Actions Implementation
description: Step where protective measures are implemented to prevent future fraud on the customer's account, including card cancellation, password reset, and security feature enablement.
context: Issued new card (old one cancelled), Reset your online banking password, Enabled extra security features

name: Police Report Filing
description: Conditional step where a police report is filed when fraud is confirmed and circumstances warrant law enforcement involvement. A reference number is generated and provided to the customer.

name: Case Documentation
description: Step where all investigation findings, actions taken, and outcomes are formally recorded in the case file for audit and compliance purposes.

name: Manager Approval for Case Closure
description: Final authorization step where a manager reviews and approves the case closure, confirming that all investigation steps have been completed and documented appropriately.

name: Closure Notification to Customer
description: Step where the customer receives formal written notification of the investigation outcome, refund details, prevention actions taken, and guidance on further protective steps they should consider.
context: We have completed our investigation into the disputed transaction

name: Fraud Investigation Manager
description: Senior role responsible for approving case closure decisions and ensuring all investigation procedures have been properly completed and documented.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: Operational team responsible for conducting fraud investigations, gathering evidence, making fraud determinations, implementing prevention measures, and communicating outcomes to customers.

name: Fraud Investigation Analyst
description: Operational staff member who gathers and analyzes evidence, makes preliminary fraud determinations, and implements prevention actions during the investigation process.

name: Fraud Determination Gate
description: Critical branching point where the investigation outcome is classified as confirmed fraud, not fraud, or inconclusive. Each determination path triggers different notification and remediation actions.

name: Refund Eligibility Check
description: Decision point determining whether a customer refund is applicable based on the fraud determination outcome. Refunds are issued when fraud is confirmed.

name: Police Report Requirement Check
description: Conditional decision point determining whether circumstances warrant filing a police report. Police reporting is triggered when fraud is confirmed and severity or circumstances justify law enforcement involvement.

name: Disputed Transaction Fraud Investigation
description: Fraud investigation case triggered by a customer's dispute of a transaction. The investigation determines whether the transaction was unauthorized fraud, authorized, or inconclusive, and implements appropriate remediation.
context: We have completed our investigation into the disputed transaction

name: Fraud Dispute Customer
description: Individual customer who has disputed a transaction on their account and is the subject of the fraud investigation and closure process. Receives investigation outcome notification and refund if applicable.
context: We have completed our investigation into the disputed transaction

name: Disputed Transaction
description: Financial transaction on the customer's account that has been disputed as unauthorized. The transaction amount and date are documented in the investigation and closure notification.
context: We have completed our investigation into the disputed transaction of £[amount] on [date]

name: Debit Card
description: Payment card associated with the customer's account that was used for the disputed fraudulent transaction. The card is cancelled and replaced as part of fraud prevention measures.

name: Replacement Card
description: New debit card issued to the customer to replace the compromised card used in the fraudulent transaction.

name: Customer Account
description: Customer's bank account on which the disputed fraudulent transaction occurred and to which the refund is issued following investigation closure.
context: Refund of £[amount] issued to your account on [date]
Review your recent statements for other unauthorized transactions

name: Fraud Prevention Procedure
description: A comprehensive operational procedure encompassing prevention actions across multiple fraud types including account takeover, card fraud, impersonation, and check fraud. The procedure defines specific controls, monitoring requirements, and customer authentication measures to mitigate fraud risk across banking channels.

name: Password Complexity Enforcement
description: A control step requiring customers to establish passwords meeting defined complexity standards as part of account takeover prevention. This step is executed during account setup and credential management.

name: Two-Factor Authentication Implementation
description: A mandatory security control implementing two-factor authentication across all customer accounts to prevent unauthorized access. This step is applied universally as part of account takeover prevention.

name: Login Anomaly Monitoring
description: A continuous monitoring step that detects and flags unusual login patterns and behaviors indicative of account compromise. This step is part of account takeover prevention controls.

name: Customer Phishing Education
description: An educational step providing customers with guidance and awareness training on phishing threats and social engineering tactics. This step supports account takeover prevention through customer awareness.

name: Chip and Contactless Card Issuance
description: A card issuance control restricting card products to chip and contactless technology only, excluding magnetic stripe cards. This step is part of card fraud prevention measures.

name: Card Transaction Alert Configuration
description: A step enabling SMS alerts to customers for card transactions exceeding a defined threshold (>£X). This step provides real-time notification of potentially fraudulent activity.

name: Card Velocity Check Implementation
description: A control step implementing transaction velocity limits to restrict the maximum number of card transactions permitted per day. This step detects and prevents rapid-fire fraudulent transaction patterns.
context: Implement velocity checks (max transactions per day)

name: High-Value Transaction Authentication
description: A step requiring explicit customer authentication and verification for card transactions above a defined value threshold. This step prevents unauthorized high-value card fraud.
context: Require customer authentication for high-value transactions

name: Enhanced KYC Verification for Impersonation Prevention
description: A strengthened Know Your Customer verification step with enhanced scrutiny to detect and prevent customer impersonation fraud. This step is part of impersonation prevention controls.

name: Original ID Document Verification Recording
description: A step requiring verification and recording of original identity documents during customer onboarding. This step creates an audit trail to detect duplicate or fraudulent identities.

name: Duplicate ID Monitoring
description: A monitoring step that detects and flags instances where the same identity document is used across multiple customer accounts. This step prevents impersonation and identity fraud.

name: Suspicious Pattern Flagging
description: A step that identifies and escalates suspicious behavioral or transactional patterns indicative of impersonation or fraud. This step supports impersonation prevention through pattern analysis.

name: Positive Pay Implementation
description: A check fraud prevention step requiring customers to pre-specify and authorize issued checks before they are cleared. This step prevents unauthorized check fraud.
context: Implement positive pay (customer specifies issued checks)

name: Large Check Verification
description: A step requiring additional verification and authentication for checks exceeding a defined value threshold. This step prevents large-value check fraud.
context: Require additional verification for large checks

name: Check Clearing Time Monitoring
description: A monitoring step that tracks check clearing times and flags unusual delays as potential indicators of check fraud. This step detects anomalies in the check clearing process.
context: Monitor check clearing times (unusual delays = red flag)

name: Fraud Prevention System
description: An automated system responsible for executing fraud prevention controls including password enforcement, 2FA implementation, anomaly monitoring, velocity checks, and pattern flagging across all fraud prevention measures.

name: Customer Service Team
description: The team responsible for educating customers on phishing threats and social engineering tactics as part of account takeover prevention measures.

name: Card Issuance Operations
description: The operational team responsible for issuing chip and contactless cards only and configuring card transaction alerts for customers.

name: KYC Verification Team
description: The team responsible for performing enhanced KYC verification, documenting original ID verification, and monitoring for duplicate identities as part of impersonation prevention.

name: Check Processing Operations
description: The operational team responsible for implementing positive pay, verifying large checks, and monitoring check clearing times as part of check fraud prevention.
context: Implement positive pay (customer specifies issued checks)
Require additional verification for large checks

name: Account Takeover Fraud Prevention
description: A fraud prevention framework addressing account takeover risks through password complexity enforcement, 2FA implementation, login anomaly monitoring, and customer phishing education.

name: Card Fraud Prevention
description: A fraud prevention framework addressing card fraud risks through chip/contactless card issuance, transaction alerts, velocity checks, and high-value transaction authentication.
context: Implement velocity checks (max transactions per day)

name: Impersonation Fraud Prevention
description: A fraud prevention framework addressing impersonation risks through enhanced KYC verification, original ID document verification recording, duplicate ID monitoring, and suspicious pattern flagging.

name: Check Fraud Prevention
description: A fraud prevention framework addressing check fraud risks through positive pay implementation, large check verification, and check clearing time monitoring.
context: Implement positive pay (customer specifies issued checks)
Require additional verification for large checks
Monitor check clearing times (unusual delays = red flag)

name: Chip Card
description: A payment card with embedded chip technology issued as part of card fraud prevention measures. Chip cards are issued exclusively, excluding magnetic stripe alternatives.

name: Contactless Card
description: A payment card with contactless technology issued as part of card fraud prevention measures. Contactless cards are issued exclusively, excluding magnetic stripe alternatives.

name: Enhanced KYC Verification
description: A strengthened Know Your Customer verification process with enhanced scrutiny applied to detect and prevent customer impersonation fraud. This process includes original ID document verification and recording.

name: Original Identity Document
description: An official identity document collected, verified, and recorded during customer onboarding as part of impersonation fraud prevention. The original document is retained to create an audit trail and detect duplicate identities.

name: High-Value Card Transaction
description: A card transaction exceeding a defined value threshold that requires explicit customer authentication and verification as part of card fraud prevention measures.
context: Require customer authentication for high-value transactions

name: Large Check Transaction
description: A check transaction exceeding a defined value threshold that requires additional verification and authentication as part of check fraud prevention measures.
context: Require additional verification for large checks

name: Fraud Investigation Process
description: End-to-end procedure for investigating suspected fraud cases, including thorough investigation before refund decisions, case file retention, confidentiality maintenance, customer notification, and implementation of preventive measures post-closure.
context: Complete investigation; only refund if confirmed/likely fraud
Retain files for 7 years minimum (supports audit trail)
Notify within 24 hours so customer can take protective action

name: Fraud Investigation Execution
description: Conduct thorough investigation of suspected fraud before making any refund decision. Refunds should only be processed if fraud is confirmed or likely.
